info.title: FlightCircle API
info.description:
## What is the Flight Circle API?

The Flight Circle API lets your application read and manage aviation data on behalf of
Flight Circle users — things like pilot profiles, aircraft, schedules, and flight records.
If you're building a third-party integration or an internal tool that connects to Flight
Circle, this is the right place to start.

## Getting Started

To use the API, you first need a `client_id` and a `client_secret`. Contact the Flight
Circle support team to register your app and receive these credentials. The
`client_secret` must be kept private — never include it in client-side code or share it
publicly.

## Basics

All API endpoints follow the form:

```
https://www.flightcircle.com/v1/api/pub/METHOD_NAME
```

- All requests must use **HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or above)**.
- Do not add a trailing slash to any URL — the server will return a `404` if you do.
- Parameters shown in curly brackets in the endpoint docs are path variables. Replace
  them with actual values: `/aircraft/{FboID}/{AircraftID}` → `/aircraft/100/200`.

## The OAuth Flow

Access to user data is controlled through OAuth 2.0 — the same "sign in with Google"
pattern you've probably seen before. The idea is simple: the user clicks a button in
your app, logs in on the Flight Circle website, and decides what your app is allowed to
see. Your app never handles their password.

The result is two tokens:

- **Access token** — a short-lived credential (expires after **1 hour**) that your app
  presents with every API request to prove it has permission. Think of it like a
  temporary pass.

- **Refresh token** — a longer-lived credential (expires after **180 days**, but the
  clock resets every time you use it) that lets your app silently obtain a new access
  token when the old one expires, without asking the user to log in again. Keep refresh
  tokens secure — treat them like passwords and never expose them to the browser or
  include them in logs.

![OAuth Flow Chart](assets/oauth-flowchart.png)

### Step 1 — Send the user to authorize

Your web or mobile app should send a GET request to:

```
GET https://www.flightcircle.com/v1/api/pub/authorize
```

Pass these query parameters:

- `client_id` — issued when you registered your app **(required)**
- `state` — a unique string you generate for this user **(optional, but strongly recommended — see below)**

Never send `client_secret` on this request.

#### Redirect URIs

For security, the URL that Flight Circle redirects the user back to after authorization
must be registered with us in advance — you cannot pass it freely in the request. Until
you register your own, the default is `http://localhost/example/server.php`, which is
useful for running the example code locally. You must register a production URI before
shipping your integration. Contact our support team to register or change your
`redirect_uri` at any time.

#### State

The `state` parameter protects against request-forgery attacks. Here's how it works:

1. Before redirecting the user, generate a value that's unique to this user and store it
   (e.g. in their session).
2. Include that value as `state` in the request to `/authorize`.
3. When Flight Circle redirects back to your app, compare the `state` you receive with
   the one you stored. If they don't match, reject the request — it may have been
   initiated by a third party.

The `state` value also gives you a convenient way to identify which user is completing
the flow, since Flight Circle will echo it back to you unchanged.

### Step 2 — Receive the temporary code

If the user approves your app, Flight Circle redirects them back to your `redirect_uri`
with a temporary `code` in the query string, plus the `state` you passed in Step 1.
Verify the `state` matches before proceeding. The code can only be used once and expires
quickly, so exchange it immediately.

### Step 3 — Exchange the code for tokens

Send a POST request to:

```
POST https://www.flightcircle.com/v1/api/pub/token
```

With these parameters:

- `client_id` — issued when you registered your app **(required)**
- `client_secret` — issued when you registered your app **(required)**
- `code` — the temporary code from Step 2
- `refresh_token` — a refresh token issued by this same endpoint

Do not pass both `code` and `refresh_token` — one of the two is required.

**Using a `code`** (first-time authorization):

```json
{
    "access_token": "0253071b6d1cce0d119cc968f6b14ceeecc3bj75",
    "refresh_token": "126f4555b483b5e8fae721b773e02fde941a785u"
}
```

**Using a `refresh_token`** (renewing an expired access token):

```json
{
    "access_token": "0253071b6d1cce0d119cc968f6b14ceeecc3bj75"
}
```

You can now use the `access_token` to call API methods on behalf of the user.

### Storing tokens and credentials

- Store `client_secret`, `access_token`, and `refresh_token` server-side only.
- Never commit them to source control or include them in client-side code.
- Encrypt tokens at rest if your storage supports it.

## Using Access Tokens

Include the access token in the `Authorization` header of every request:

```
GET /v1/api/pub/user/describe
Authorization: Bearer 0253071b6d1cce0d119cc968f6b14ceeecc3bj75
```

**cURL example:**

```bash
curl https://www.flightcircle.com/v1/api/pub/user/describe \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer 0253071b6d1cce0d119cc968f6b14ceeecc3bj75"
```

Avoid passing the token as a query string parameter — query strings appear in server
logs and browser history, which can expose the token unintentionally.

## Scopes

When authorizing your app, the user grants it one or more scopes that control what data
can be accessed:

| Scope | What it allows | Who can grant it |
|-------|----------------|-----------------|
| `user` | Read the authenticated user's own profile and data | Any user |
| `fbo` | Read the FBO's data (aircraft, schedules, members, etc.) | FBO admin only |
| `write` | Create, update, and delete records | FBO admin only |

Request only the scopes your app actually needs.

## Rate Limits

The API allows up to **100 requests per minute** per access token. Exceeding this limit
returns a `429 Too Many Requests` response. If you hit the limit, wait until the next
minute window before retrying.

## Errors

Errors are returned as plain text with a semantically correct HTTP status code. For
example, a missing required parameter returns `400 Bad Request`, and an expired token
returns `401 Unauthorized`. Check the status code first, then read the response body
for a human-readable explanation.

## Dates

Dates are not yet consistently formatted across all endpoints. We are working to
standardise them all to ISO 8601 (e.g. `2024-06-15T14:30:00Z`). Until then, treat date
formats as endpoint-specific and check the individual endpoint documentation.

## Pagination

Endpoints that return lists do not currently support pagination — all results are
returned at once. Pagination is planned for a future release.

## Status & Versioning

The Flight Circle API is currently in **beta**. Endpoints, parameters, and response
shapes may change without prior notice while we iterate. Once the API reaches maturity
we will notify all registered integrations at least a couple of weeks before any
breaking change is introduced.

## Example Code

The example below shows how to authenticate and call the `/user/describe` endpoint.
[Download the example code](assets/example.zip) — it contains three PHP files:
`client.php`, `server.php`, and `describe_user.php`.

1. Make sure you have a local web server running (e.g. Apache or Nginx).
2. Extract the zip into a folder named `example` at the root of your web server, so
   that `client.php` is accessible at `http://localhost/example/client.php`.
3. In `client.php`, set `$client_id` to your Client ID.
4. In `server.php`, set both `$client_id` and `$client_secret` to your credentials.
5. Open `http://localhost/example/client.php` in your browser.
6. You will be redirected to the Flight Circle login page. Log in and authorize the app.
7. You will be redirected back to `http://localhost/example/server.php`, which will
   automatically exchange the code for a token and display it.
8. Click "Describe user to test token" — this calls `/user/describe` using your new
   token and displays your profile data.

If any step fails, contact our support team with the details.

Once you are ready to move beyond local testing, register your production `redirect_uri`
with us before going live.

scopes.user: Read the authenticated user's own profile and data
scopes.fbo: Read the FBO's data (aircraft, schedules, members, etc.)

InstructorID.name: InstructorID
InstructorID.description: Instructor identifier, or the literal string `"all"` to include all instructors.

GenericID.name: ID
GenericID.description:
Either a numeric AircraftID (returns all records for that aircraft) or a
hash-string record ID (returns the single matching record).

AircraftList.name: AircraftList
AircraftList.description: Comma-separated list of AircraftIDs, or the literal string `"all"`.

ServicesList.name: ServicesList
ServicesList.description: Comma-separated list of ServiceIDs, or the literal string `"all"`.

UsersList.name: UsersList
UsersList.description: Comma-separated list of UserIDs, or the literal string `"all"`.

CustomFieldValue.description: Value of a custom field. Boolean fields are returned as the string "Yes" or "No".

custom_fields.description:
Dynamic map of custom field name → value. Boolean fields are "Yes"/"No".
Only fields configured as visible by the FBO are included.

UserDescribeList.description:
One entry per FBO the authenticated user belongs to.
Returned by the no-`FboID` describe variants.

UserListItem.description: Full customer record as returned by listAll.

balance.description: Account balance rounded to 2 decimal places.

file_categories.description: Active file categories configured for this user.

medical_class.description:
Allowed values depend on the FBO's aviation authority. FAA base set:
`Class 1`, `Class 2`, `Class 3`, `BasicMed`, `Military`, `Other`,
`Sport Pilot (Drivers License)`. CASA adds `Basic Class 2`.

certificate_type.description:
Allowed values depend on the FBO's aviation authority. Base set:
`Student`, `Sport`, `Recreational`, `Private`, `Commercial`, `ATP`.
EASA adds `SPL`, `LAPLA`, `LAPLS`, `PPL`.

craft_categories.description:
Each entry must be one of the allowed values for the FBO's aviation
authority. FAA base set: `Airplane`, `Rotocraft`, `Powered Lift`,
`Glider`, `Lighter-than-air`, `Weight-Shift Control`. EASA adds `TMG`.

class_ratings.description:
FBO-authority dependent enum. Base set includes `Single Engine Land`,
`Single Engine Sea`, `Multi Engine Land`, `Multi Engine Sea`,
`Helicopter`, `Gyroplane`, `Airship`, `Gas Balloon`, `Hot Air Balloon`,
`Weight-Shift Control: Land`, `Weight-Shift Control: Sea`. EASA adds
`TMG`, `Gliders`.

endorsements.description:
FBO-authority dependent enum. Base set: `Tailwheel`, `High Performance`,
`Complex`, `Solo`, `Pressurized`, `Ground-tow`, `Aero-tow`,
`Self-launch`. EASA and CASA each extend the list.

other_ratings.description:
FBO-authority dependent enum. Base set: `Instrument Airplane`,
`Instrument Helicopter`, `Instrument Powered Lift`, `Night (EASA)`,
`Small Unmanned Aircraft System`. EASA adds `Towing`,
`TMG Night Rating`, `Aerobatic`.

CreateUserRequest.description:
Combined user + customer create payload. Accepts both user and customer
profile fields.

Notes:
- If `email` is omitted or empty, a random `@flightcircle.com` address is
  generated server-side.
- If `send_customer_verification_email` is `1`, a welcome/verification
  email is dispatched after the user is created.

send_customer_verification_email.description:
When `1`, the server dispatches a verification email to the new
customer. Defaults to no email if omitted.

UpdateCustomerRequest.description:
Partial update of a customer profile. Only include fields you wish to
change; omitted fields are left untouched. All fields are optional.

expires.description: Expiration date/time in UTC. null if the file never expires.

url.description: Relative URL to the download endpoint for this file.

UploadFileJsonBody.description: Optional metadata fields passed inside the `data` JSON string when uploading via multipart.

name.description:
Display name for the file. Defaults to the filename stem
(e.g. "invoice" for "invoice.pdf") if not provided.

expires.description:
Expiration date/time. Accepts ISO 8601 date ("2030-06-15") or
datetime ("2030-06-15T14:30:00Z", "2030-06-15T14:30:00-05:00").
Date-only values are interpreted as end-of-day in the FBO's timezone.
Stored internally as a UTC Unix timestamp.

FileID.description: Identifier of the newly created file record.

UpdateFileRequest.description: Partial update — at least one of `name`, `categories`, or `expires` must be provided.

name.description: New display name for the file.

oneOf.description: Array of category strings. Joined into a comma-separated string.

expires.description:
New expiration date/time. Accepts ISO 8601 date ("2030-06-15") or
datetime ("2030-06-15T14:30:00Z", "2030-06-15T14:30:00-05:00").
Date-only values are interpreted as end-of-day in the FBO's timezone.
Pass an empty string to clear expiration.

hourly_rate.description: Hourly rental rate. May be "NaN" if not configured.

photo.description: Filename of the aircraft photo, or null.

label.description: Reminder label / type (e.g. "meter required at", "date required at").

last.description: Last service value (Unix timestamp or meter reading).

next.description: Next service threshold (Unix timestamp or meter value).

MaintenanceRemindersResponse.description:
Maintenance reminders split into two groups: upcoming (`reminders`) and
past-due / expired (`expired`).

aircraft_checkouts.description: List of aircraft IDs this instructor is checked out on.

cancelled_by.description: Full name of the user who cancelled.

resource.description: Name of the resource (aircraft or other) that was booked.

LedgerItem.description:
A single ledger entry. Entries sharing the same `InvoiceID` belong to the
same transaction.

**To get payments:** filter by `entry_type == "Payment"`. Include
`entry_type == "Adjustment"` with `adjustment_type == "Credit"` for credits.

**To get charges:** filter by `entry_type == "Charge"`. Include
`entry_type == "Adjustment"` with `adjustment_type == "Debit"` for debits.

InvoiceID.description: Invoice identifier (numeric string or hash string).

amount.description: Total charge for this entry (quantity × unit price + taxes + global taxes).

aircraft.description: List of AircraftIDs this service applies to.

User.description: Full name of the user who logged the entry.

403Forbidden.description: Not authorized. The authenticated user lacks permission for this operation.

404NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

400BadRequest.description: Bad request. Invalid input or business rule violation.

422UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed. Response body lists each failing assertion.

429TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the current rate limit window resets.

get.summary: Describe the authenticated user across all FBOs
get.description:
Returns one profile entry per FBO the authenticated user belongs to,
each including custom fields scoped to that FBO. Returns an empty array
if the user has no active customer records.

200.description: One profile per FBO the user belongs to.

get.summary: Describe the authenticated user scoped to an FBO
get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's profile with custom fields scoped to the
given FBO. The `FboID` must match the API key's FBO (or the API key must
have cross-FBO access).

get.summary: List all customers for an FBO
get.description:
Returns a full list of customers registered with the given FBO, including
profile data, certificates, medical records, files, and custom fields.

The caller must be an employee of `FboID`. Results are ordered by status
(DESC) then last name (ASC). Dates and times are returned in the FBO's
configured timezone.

post.description:
Creates a new user account and associated customer record for the FBO
identified by the API key.

**Rate limit:** Returns 409 if more than 200 customers are created within
a 24-hour window for the same FBO.

A random password is generated automatically; a welcome/verification email
is dispatched asynchronously.

422.description:
Validation failure or business-rule violation. Covers field validation
failures, duplicate email, and the daily creation cap (more than
200 customers created in the last 24 hours for this FBO).

500.description: Unexpected server error. Body is a plain-text message.

put.description: Updates a customer profile. Any subset of profile fields may be provided.

422.description:
Validation failure or business-rule violation — e.g. invalid field
value or the target user is not a customer of this FBO.

500.description: Unexpected server error. Body is a plain-text message.

get.summary: List files for a user
get.description:
Returns all files associated with the given user and the FBO of the API key.
The caller must be an employee of that FBO, and the user must be an active
customer (status ≠ 0).

Timestamps are returned in UTC ISO 8601 format. Categories are returned as
an array of strings. The `url` field in each item points to the download
endpoint for that file.

post.summary: Upload a file for a user
post.description:
Uploads a file and attaches it to the given user record.

Send a `multipart/form-data` request with:
- `file`: the binary file payload.
- `data`: a JSON string containing optional metadata fields
  (`name`, `categories`, `expires`).

**Allowed file extensions:**
`.txt`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.png`, `.doc`, `.docx`, `.xls`,
`.xlsx`, `.pdf`, `.csv`, `.numbers`, `.webp`, `.ozacft`, `.pptx`, `.zip`

403.description:
Not authorized. Either the token lacks the required scope, the caller
is not an employee of this FBO, or the target user is not an active
customer of this FBO.

422.description:
Validation failed. Possible causes:
- No file provided
- `filename` exceeds 255 characters
- `name` exceeds 255 characters
- File extension not in the allowed list
- `expires` is not a valid ISO 8601 date/time
- File is empty or unreadable

500.description: Unexpected server error. Body is a plain-text message.

get.summary: Download a file
get.description:
Redirects to a signed S3 URL for the requested file. The signed URL
expires shortly after issuance — follow the redirect immediately.

The file must belong to the FBO of the API key and the specified user.

302.description: Redirect to signed S3 download URL.

put.description:
Updates one or more metadata fields of an existing file record.
The file content itself is not changed.

At least one of `name`, `categories`, or `expires` must be provided.

`expires` accepts ISO 8601 date (`"2030-06-15"`) or datetime
(`"2030-06-15T14:30:00-05:00"`). Date-only values are resolved to
end-of-day in the FBO's configured timezone, then stored as a UTC
Unix timestamp.

404.description: File not found or does not belong to this FBO/user.

500.description: Unexpected server error. Body is a plain-text message.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the file record and the underlying S3 object.
This operation is irreversible.

The file must belong to the FBO of the API key and the specified user.

404.description: File not found or does not belong to this FBO/user.

500.description: Unexpected server error. Body is a plain-text message.

get.summary: Start the OAuth authorization flow
get.description:
Redirects the user to the Flight Circle login and authorization page.
This endpoint is browser-facing — your app should redirect the user's
browser to this URL, not call it from a server.

If the user is not logged in they will see a login form first. After
logging in (or if already authenticated) they will be shown an
authorization page where they can approve or deny your app's access.

On approval, Flight Circle redirects the user back to your registered
`redirect_uri` with a temporary `code` and the `state` you passed in.
That code must be exchanged immediately at `POST /token`.

Note: unlike standard OAuth 2.0, `redirect_uri` is not a parameter here.
Flight Circle uses the URI you registered with our support team. If none
has been registered, it defaults to `http://localhost/example/server.php`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Your app's Client ID, issued when you registered with Flight Circle.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
A unique value you generate for this user (e.g. a random token stored
in their session). Flight Circle echoes it back unchanged. Use it to
verify the callback is genuine and to identify which user is completing
the flow. Strongly recommended.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
Space-separated list of scopes to request. Defaults to `user` if omitted.
Example: `user fbo` or `user fbo write`. See the **Scopes** section for
available values and who can grant each one.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: Must be `code` if provided. Defaults to `code` automatically.

302.description:
Redirects to the Flight Circle authorization page (or login page if
the user is not authenticated). On completion the user is redirected
back to your `redirect_uri` with `code` and `state` query parameters.

post.summary: Issue or refresh an access token
post.description:
Exchanges an authorization `code` for an `access_token` and a
`refresh_token`, or exchanges a `refresh_token` for a new `access_token`.

Also available at `POST /access_token` (legacy alias — prefer `/token`).

The `grant_type` field is optional: the server defaults to
`authorization_code` when `code` is present and retries with
`refresh_token` automatically when the code exchange fails.

client_secret.description: Your app's Client Secret. Never expose this client-side.

code.description:
The temporary authorization code received from `GET /authorize`.
Provide either `code` or `refresh_token`, not both.

refresh_token.description:
A refresh token previously issued by this endpoint.
Provide either `code` or `refresh_token`, not both.

grant_type.description:
Defaults to `authorization_code` when omitted. Set to
`refresh_token` when exchanging a refresh token.

access_token.description: Bearer token to include in API requests. Expires after 1 hour.

refresh_token.description:
Token to obtain a new access token without re-authorizing the user.
Expires after 180 days; expiry resets on each use.
Only returned when exchanging an authorization `code`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

500.description: Invalid or expired code / refresh token.

get.summary: List all aircraft for an FBO
get.description: Returns all active aircraft registered to the given FBO.

get.summary: Get a single aircraft
get.description: Returns the aircraft record for the given AircraftID within the FBO.

200.description: Array containing the matching aircraft record.

get.summary: List all open squawks for an FBO
get.description: Returns all open squawks across all aircraft for the given FBO.

get.summary: Get squawks by aircraft or squawk ID
get.description:
Filters squawks by ID. The `{ID}` parameter is dual-purpose:
- **Numeric AircraftID** — returns all squawks for that aircraft.
- **Hash-string SquawkID** — returns the single matching squawk.

get.summary: List all maintenance reminders for an FBO
get.description:
Returns all maintenance reminders split into upcoming (`reminders`) and
past-due (`expired`).

get.summary: Get maintenance reminders by aircraft or reminder ID
get.description:
Filters maintenance reminders by ID. The `{ID}` parameter is dual-purpose:
- **Numeric AircraftID** — returns all reminders for that aircraft.
- **Hash-string ReminderID** — returns the single matching reminder.

Response structure is identical to the FBO-wide list.

200.description: Reminders and expired items for the given aircraft or reminder.

get.summary: List all instructors for an FBO
get.description: Returns all instructors registered with the given FBO.

get.summary: Get a single instructor
get.description: Returns the instructor record for the given InstructorID within the FBO.

200.description: Array containing the matching instructor record.

get.summary: List instructor schedules
get.description:
Returns reservations for the given instructor within a date range.

`InstructorID` may be the literal string `"all"` to return schedules for
all instructors.

**Date segments are optional from the right.** The server supports truncated
paths — you may omit trailing segments:
- `/schedules/{FboID}/{InstructorID}` — returns today and tomorrow.
- `/schedules/{FboID}/{InstructorID}/{year}` — returns today and tomorrow
  (year alone acts as the today/tomorrow shortcut).
- `/schedules/{FboID}/{InstructorID}/{year}/{month}/{day}` — returns from
  that start date with no defined end.
- Full path — returns the range from start to end date (inclusive).

get.summary: List checked-in flights
get.description:
Returns flight records (checked-in reservations) for the given FBO within
the specified date range. Only flights that have been checked in are
returned.

get.summary: List cancelled reservations
get.description:
Returns cancelled reservation records for the given FBO within the
specified date range. The caller must have super admin role or be in a
group with Cancellations report access.

get.summary: List ledger entries for a user
get.description:
Returns ledger entries for the given user within the specified date range.
The caller must have admin role or be in a group with ledger read access.

Entries sharing the same `InvoiceID` belong to the same transaction. See
`LedgerItem` for guidance on filtering payments vs. charges.

get.summary: List store items for an FBO
get.description: Returns all store items (products/services) configured for the given FBO.

get.summary: List adjustments for an FBO
get.description: Returns all adjustment types (credits and debits) configured for the given FBO.

get.summary: Get next upcoming reservation for the FBO
get.description:
Returns the next reservation within the next 2 days for any user in the
given FBO.

200.description: Array of upcoming reservation records (may be empty).

get.summary: Get next upcoming reservation for a user
get.description:
Returns the next reservation within the next 2 days for the given user
in the given FBO.

200.description: Array containing the next reservation, or empty if none.

get.summary: List reservations for a user
get.description:
Returns reservations for the given user within a date range.

`UserID` may be the literal string `"all"` to return schedules across all
users for the FBO.

**Date segments are optional from the right.** The server supports truncated
paths — you may omit trailing segments:
- `/user/schedules/{FboID}/{UserID}` — returns today and tomorrow.
- `/user/schedules/{FboID}/{UserID}/{year}` — returns today and tomorrow
  (year alone acts as the today/tomorrow shortcut).
- `/user/schedules/{FboID}/{UserID}/{year}/{month}/{day}` — returns from
  that start date with no defined end.
- Full path — returns the range from start to end date (inclusive).

get.summary: List service types for an FBO
get.description: Returns all services tracked definitions configured for the given FBO.

get.summary: Query services tracked log
get.description:
Returns service log entries matching the given filters and date range.
All path parameters are required.

Use `"all"` for `AircraftList`, `ServicesList`, or `UsersList` to include
all records for that dimension without filtering.

tags.name: User Files
tags.description: File upload, download, and metadata management for users.

tags.name: Aircraft
tags.description: Aircraft records, squawks, and maintenance reminders.

tags.name: Flights
tags.description: Reservations, instructor schedules, checked-in flight records, and instructor information.
